name: 03_tree_and_tools
title: A folder tree that cascades, and one tool of each kind
why: Owner's requests on the wiztry11 exe, 2026-11-12: (1) clicking a block brings up the file in the tree, but not the folders that lead to it; the folders should cascade down from the root and stay organized. (2) Add the other things WizTree has, like delete: one of each kind is enough. Found in the code: select_node adds a missing folder as a NEW ROW AT THE TOP of the tree, cut off from its parents; folders below the first level get no arrow and the open handler does nothing, so the tree cannot be opened downward at all; nothing is bound to double-click (the spec's zoom on double-click was never built; the old test only called zoom()); % of Parent shows the share of the whole scan and does not use bar(). Tools chosen, one per kind: changes the disk = Delete to the Recycle Bin (asked first, guarded); starts another program = Show in Explorer; clipboard = Copy path; writes a report = Export to CSV.
proved: 2026-11-12: on a scratch copy, in order and each alone: T11 (32 checks), T12 (36 checks, with real deletes to the Recycle Bin inside a temp folder), T13 (37 checks); after each, every older test still passes, and at the end all 13 test files pass including the exe build. On the wiztry11 build each new test fails for the reasons above.
rules: Read-only: the app never deletes, moves, renames or writes any file it scans.

Scanning is read-only: it never deletes, moves, renames or writes anything. The ONLY code that may remove anything is trash() in wiztry/actions.py, which moves one item to the Recycle Bin after the person said Yes, and only inside the scanned folder. No os.remove, os.unlink, os.rmdir, shutil.rmtree, shutil.move, os.rename or shell delete anywhere in wiztry/, ever. To try a delete yourself, make your own folder with tempfile.mkdtemp() and delete only inside it.
Standard library only in wiztry/ (tkinter, os, stat, threading, json, argparse, dataclasses, datetime, time). PyInstaller is only for build.bat.
Standard library only in wiztry/ (tkinter, os, stat, threading, json, argparse, dataclasses, datetime, time, csv, ctypes, subprocess). PyInstaller is only for build.bat.
Import between modules as `from wiztry.<module> import <names>`; never copy code from another module.

Import between modules as `from wiztry.<module> import <names>`; never copy code from another module. One exception: wiztry/app.py reaches the tools as `import wiztry.actions as actions` and calls them as actions.trash(...), actions.show_in_explorer(...), so they can be swapped in a test.
spec: It is read-only: it never deletes, moves, renames or writes any file it scans. No admin rights.

Scanning is read-only: it never deletes, moves, renames or writes any file it scans. The one thing that changes the disk is Delete in the right-click menu: it asks first and moves the item to the Recycle Bin. No admin rights.
spec_add:
## Tree and tools (added 2026-11-12)
- The folder tree always starts at the scanned folder. Every folder with something in it can be opened, level by level. Clicking a block in the treemap opens every folder on the way to that file, selects it and scrolls to it. Double-clicking a folder row zooms the treemap into it.
- Right-click on a tree row or a treemap block: Show in Explorer, Copy path, Delete (Recycle Bin)... The Delete key does the same as Delete. Delete asks first, refuses the scanned folder itself, drives and anything outside the scanned folder, and afterwards the tree, the file types and the treemap show the new sizes without a new scan.
- Export... in the toolbar writes the tree as a CSV file: Path, Type, Size, Files, Folders, Modified.

tasks.title: A folder tree that cascades
tasks.brief:
The folder tree is broken below its first level: folders have no arrow, opening one shows nothing, and select_node puts a missing folder in as a new row at the TOP of the tree. Rebuild the tree code in wiztry/app.py around five small methods; change nothing else in the window. Every check in tests/test_app.py, tests/test_window_use.py and tests/test_window_big.py must keep passing.

State: self.nodes = {row id: Node} as now, plus self.items = {id(node): row id} (the other direction, so a Node's row is found without searching). Both are emptied whenever the tree is emptied and always change together.

1. _add_row(parent_iid, node): insert ONE row under parent_iid (text = node.name, closed, values = self._row_values(node)), record it in self.nodes and self.items, and, when node is a folder with children, insert one empty placeholder child row (text "") that is NOT recorded in self.nodes: it is what gives the folder its arrow. Returns the row id.
2. _fill_row(iid): the row's Node from self.nodes (not a folder -> return). If the row's first child is already in self.nodes it has been filled: return. Otherwise delete its children (the placeholder) and _add_row every child of the Node, in the order of node.children (they are sorted largest first already).
3. _fill_tree(top): empty the tree, self.nodes and self.items; _add_row("", top); _fill_row that row; open it. This is the ONLY place a row is inserted at the top level (parent "").
4. The <<TreeviewOpen>> handler: self._fill_row(self.tree.focus()). Nothing else (do not test whether the row is open: it already is when the event arrives).
5. select_node(node): walk up from node through .parent collecting the Nodes that have no row yet, until one that has a row (none found -> return None). Going back down, _fill_row the row of each one's parent, so each gets its row in place. Then open every ancestor row of node's row (self.tree.item(row, open=True), going up with self.tree.parent), selection_set, focus and see the row, and return its id. Never insert a row here.

Also:
- _row_values: % of Parent is the share of the row's OWN parent: node.size / node.parent.size * 100 (100.0 for the scanned folder itself; 0.0 when the parent's size is 0), shown as bar(pct) - the bar() function at the top of app.py.
- zoom_row(iid): if that row's Node is a folder, self.zoom(node); a file row changes nothing. Bind <Double-1> on the tree to a handler that calls self.zoom_row(self.tree.identify_row(event.y)).
- A click on a treemap block keeps doing select_node(node) and must not change self.view.
- show_result keeps calling _fill_tree(top) for a new result; remove the old row code that these methods replace (_insert_tree_item, _open_placeholder).

tasks.title: The tools: Recycle Bin, Explorer, CSV
tasks.brief:
A new module wiztry/actions.py with the tools the window will offer. Standard library only (csv, ctypes, datetime, os, subprocess). It is the only place in the app that can remove anything, and it has exactly one way to do it: the Recycle Bin. The words os.remove, os.unlink, os.rmdir, rmtree, os.rename, os.replace and shutil.move must not appear anywhere in the file, not even in a comment.

- can_delete(path: str, root: str) -> str: "" when path may be deleted, otherwise the reason, exactly one of these strings, tested in this order. Compare on p = os.path.normcase(os.path.abspath(path)).rstrip("\\") and r = the same of root. (1) path empty or only spaces -> "no path". (2) p is a drive letter and a colon -> "a drive". (3) p == r -> "the scanned folder itself". (4) p does not start with r + "\\" -> "outside the scanned folder". (5) not os.path.lexists(path) -> "not found".
- trash(path: str, root: str) -> None: why = can_delete(path, root); if why: raise ValueError(why). Then move it to the Recycle Bin with SHFileOperationW through ctypes: a ctypes.Structure SHFILEOPSTRUCTW with the fields hwnd (HWND), wFunc (UINT), pFrom (LPCWSTR), pTo (LPCWSTR), fFlags (c_uint16), fAnyOperationsAborted (BOOL), hNameMappings (c_void_p), lpszProgressTitle (LPCWSTR); wFunc = FO_DELETE = 3; pFrom = os.path.abspath(path) + "\0" (the list of names ends with a second NUL, which ctypes adds); fFlags = FOF_ALLOWUNDO (0x0040) | FOF_NOCONFIRMATION (0x0010) | FOF_SILENT (0x0004) | FOF_NOERRORUI (0x0400), each a named module constant. Call ctypes.windll.shell32.SHFileOperationW(ctypes.byref(op)); a result other than 0, or fAnyOperationsAborted set, -> raise OSError with a short message. A folder goes with everything in it.
- forget(node) -> None: after a delete, take the Node out of the tree in memory: remove it from node.parent.children, then for every folder from the parent up to the top subtract node.size from size, node.files from files, and node.folders (plus 1 if node is a folder) from folders. A Node without a parent: do nothing.
- explorer_args(path: str) -> list: ["explorer.exe", "/select,", path]. show_in_explorer(path: str) -> None: subprocess.Popen(explorer_args(path)). Never call show_in_explorer while you work: it opens a window on the person's desktop. Check explorer_args instead.
- export_csv(top, file: str) -> int: write file with the csv module, encoding "utf-8-sig", newline="". Header row: Path, Type, Size, Files, Folders, Modified. Then one row for top and one for every Node under it: a folder is followed directly by its contents, in the order of .children (largest first). Use an explicit stack, not recursion. Columns: node.path; "Folder" or "File"; node.size; node.files; node.folders (0 for a file); the mtime as %Y-%m-%d %H:%M, or "" when mtime is 0. Returns the number of rows written, not counting the header.

To try trash() yourself, make a folder with tempfile.mkdtemp() and delete only inside it, the way tests/test_actions.py does.

tasks.title: The right-click menu and Export
tasks.brief:
Wire the tools of wiztry/actions.py into the window (wiztry/app.py only). Every older test must keep passing.

Imports at the top of app.py: `import tkinter.messagebox` (tk.messagebox does not exist until it is imported) and `import wiztry.actions as actions`. Always call the tools through the module, as actions.trash(...), actions.can_delete(...), actions.forget(...), actions.show_in_explorer(...), actions.export_csv(...), and the dialogs as tkinter.messagebox.askyesno(...) and tkinter.filedialog.asksaveasfilename(...): the test swaps them.

1. self.menu = tk.Menu(self, tearoff=0) with exactly three commands, in this order and with these labels: "Show in Explorer" -> self.show_in_explorer, "Copy path" -> self.copy_path, "Delete (Recycle Bin)..." -> self.delete_selected.
2. Right-click (<Button-3>) on the tree: the row under the pointer (self.tree.identify_row(event.y)), if it is in self.nodes, is selected and focused, then self.menu.tk_popup(event.x_root, event.y_root). Right-click on the treemap canvas: node = self.node_at(event.x, event.y); if there is one, self.select_node(node), then the same popup. Bind <Delete> on the tree to delete_selected. Never call tk_popup while you work or in a test: it waits for a person.
3. selected_node(): the Node of the selected tree row (self.nodes of the first selected row), or None.
4. copy_path(): nothing selected -> return. Otherwise clipboard_clear(), clipboard_append(node.path), status f"Copied: {node.path}".
5. show_in_explorer(): nothing selected -> return. Otherwise actions.show_in_explorer(node.path).
6. delete_selected() -> bool, True only when the item went to the Recycle Bin:
   - nothing selected or no scan yet -> return False.
   - why = actions.can_delete(node.path, self.top.path); if why: status f"Cannot delete: {why}", return False (without asking).
   - ask tkinter.messagebox.askyesno("WizTry", f"Move this to the Recycle Bin?\n\n{node.path}\n{human(node.size)}", parent=self); No -> return False.
   - try actions.trash(node.path, self.top.path); on OSError or ValueError as e: status f"Could not delete: {e}", return False, and change nothing else.
   - Then bring everything up to date WITHOUT a new scan, in this order: (a) gone = the by_ext of what was deleted: summary(node)["by_ext"] for a folder (summary and ext_of are in wiztry.scanner), {ext_of(node.name): {"size": node.size, "files": 1}} for a file. (b) remember parent = node.parent and the node's row id, then actions.forget(node). (c) remove the row and every row inside it from self.nodes and self.items (walk the row's children with an explicit stack), then self.tree.delete(row). (d) for every folder from parent up to the top that has a row: set the row's values again with self._row_values, and also the values of its child rows that are in self.nodes (their % of Parent changed); if the folder now has no children, delete its leftover child rows. (e) subtract gone from self.by_ext (size and files per extension; delete an extension whose files reach 0), then self.colors = color_map(self.by_ext) and fill the File Types list from self.by_ext. For this, show_result must keep the by_ext it is given as self.by_ext. (f) if self.view is the deleted Node or inside it (walk up from self.view through .parent), self.view = self.top. (g) self.draw_treemap(). (h) status f"Moved to the Recycle Bin: {node.name} ({human(node.size)})"; return True.
7. export(): no scan yet -> return. file = tkinter.filedialog.asksaveasfilename(parent=self, defaultextension=".csv", filetypes=[("CSV", "*.csv")]); "" -> return. rows = actions.export_csv(self.top, file); status f"Exported {rows:,} rows to {file}". Add a ttk.Button "Export..." to the toolbar, after Top, that calls self.export.
